result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_louvain()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using Louvain multi-level optimization algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13868-L14009){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_louvain( resolution=1.0, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Louvain communities](/assets/graphs/cmty-louvain.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the single edge C to D. Louvain puts each cluster in its own community, drawn as tinted regions in teal and the accent color. The card lists community 0 as D, E, F, G and community 1 as A, B, C." width="100%"} The Louvain method is a hierarchical algorithm that maximizes modularity through iterative optimization. It's the most widely-used community detection algorithm in practice due to its speed (`O(n log n)`) and quality on large networks. The method produces a dendrogram hierarchy but returns the partition with maximum modularity. Works only with undirected graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Resolution parameter controlling community size. Higher values favor smaller communities. Standard modularity uses resolution=1.0. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_louvain`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed, contiguous). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Louvain (Blondel et al., 2008) alternates two phases until modularity converges. In the local phase, each node greedily joins the neighboring community that offers the highest modularity gain $\Delta Q$, computed in $O(1)$ per move from precomputed community sums. In the aggregation phase, every community collapses to a single super-node and the process restarts on the reduced graph, which is what lets Louvain reach coarse community structure in near-linear time. The `resolution=` parameter multiplies the null-model term inside $\Delta Q$: values below $1$ merge communities more aggressively (larger, fewer groups), values above $1$ resist merges (smaller, more numerous groups), and the default of $1$ recovers standard modularity. Louvain is deterministic given a fixed node ordering, but different orderings can produce equally valid alternative partitions. Disconnected components are handled naturally; self-loops and multi-edges are not currently supported. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Nodes within each triangle end up in the same community, and the two triangles get different communities, since the bridge edge is the only thing connecting them: ::: {#0e5f42b5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") ) # Build two complete triangles connected by bridge for i, j in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) graph.add_edge("C", "D") # Bridge for i, j in [("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) communities = graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): cid for nid, cid in communities.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'C': 1, 'A': 1, 'E': 0, 'F': 0, 'D': 0, 'B': 1} ``` ::: ::: Raising `resolution=` above `1.0` favors smaller communities, and lowering it below `1.0` favors larger ones: ::: {#f036e19b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} fine = graph.cmty_louvain(resolution=1.5, return_dict=True) coarse = graph.cmty_louvain(resolution=0.5, return_dict=True) len(set(fine.values())), len(set(coarse.values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (2, 2) ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute and chaining into `colorize_node_attrs()` visualizes the communities directly: ::: {#794e1c65 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="E") .add_edge(source="E", target="F") .add_edge(source="F", target="D") ) ( graph .cmty_louvain(attr_name="community") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="viridis") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 6 Number of edges : 7 Directed : False Density : 0.47 Average degree (min, max) : 2.33 (2, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations on nodes: - cmty_louvain() -> attr: 'community' (6 of 6 nodes) Node aesthetics: - color <- community via colorize (palette: "viridis") (values: #440154, #482777, 6 of 6 nodes) ``` ::: :::
